phase_E: Physically separate client (R2-6): the Mac (Apple M4, macOS 27) runs the phase A protocol as client of the benchmark host's databases over the LAN, Wi-Fi at both ends (host wlp3s0 2.4 GHz, power saving off; the host's Ethernet port is down; no wired adapter). Same database host, SF1 data (fingerprints before and after per engine), source snapshot, inputs, index states, server settings and result policy as phase A; runner code/rc_e.py subclasses the phase A runner with --client-mode separate-client.
phase_E_cells: Q6, Q17, Q18, Q20, Q21 x 4 engines x 2 index states x 2 frameworks, except the five SF1 host-censored query cells (PostgreSQL non-indexed Q17/Q20/Q21, MySQL non-indexed Q17/Q20): 35 query cells, 70 framework cells, 8 blocks each.
phase_E_client: Pinned client container rcg-client:3.12.3 (Python 3.12.3, the host venv's package versions; linux/arm64; 2 CPUs on VM vCPUs 2-3, 3 GB), as phase G v2; recorded per run with the Mac model and macOS version. The host client in phase A is /usr/bin/python3.12 on x86_64 Ubuntu pinned to CPUs 2-3. E versus A is therefore the combined observed change of network, client machine, OS and architecture, not pure network overhead (brief, part E).
phase_E_host_evidence: bench-host verify and Oracle process affinity read over ssh immediately before (recorded in the run inventory and gated as in phase A) and after every run; the host must run no other campaign unit.
phase_E_network: Per run: ping summary (60 x 0.5 s) before and after, a 1 s ping log during the run, the Mac's and the host's Wi-Fi link (PHY mode, channel, rate, signal/noise; no network name or hardware address). Not part of any timing.
phase_E_oracle_cancellation: Oracle runs only with V$SESSION readable (root helper action oracle-session-view; gated): the /proc fallback of the same-host runner sees no Oracle processes from the client.
phase_E_order: Per engine: host plan E-<engine>-a, root action, reachability, network cancellation pilot, the separate-client trial (first engine only; must pass before the long run), first index state, host plan E-<engine>-b, second state, host plan E-<engine>-c, undo of the root action. Engines in the order the host leaves them: Oracle, Commercial System A, PostgreSQL, MySQL.
phase_E_driver: code/rc_e_driver.sh: resumable step markers in E-client/steps; a watchdog kills a client whose progress file has not moved for 25 minutes (a dead socket over Wi-Fi can block past the 900 s statement limit) and the run resumes, up to three attempts; a refused gate, failed end checks or a fatal record stop the driver instead.
